# Drives the "Apple Pay certificate" workflow. Edit and commit to run it.
#
# Before anything here works:
#   1. Shopify must approve write_mobile_payments and read_mobile_payments for the store.
#   2. SHOPIFY_CLIENT_ID and SHOPIFY_CLIENT_SECRET must be repository secrets (Settings →
#      Secrets and variables → Actions), taken from the app's API credentials at
#      dev.shopify.com. Never paste them into a file — this one is public in the repo.
#
# There is no permanent token to store any more. Shopify retired admin-created custom apps
# ("You can no longer create these apps"), so the workflow mints a token per run with the
# client credentials grant, which is the one Shopify names for server-side integrations acting
# on their own store. Those tokens last 24 hours, which is why storing one would have worked
# for a day and then quietly stopped.
#
# # First run with real credentials. status is a read: it authenticates with the client
# credentials grant and lists whatever certificates the store already has. If the token comes
# back, the app and secrets are wired correctly; if the certificates call is then rejected,
# that is the scope approval still pending, which is a different and expected failure.
action=status   list the certificates the store already has (safe; start here)
# action=create   make a resource, wait for the CSR, print it and attach it as an artifact
# action=upload   send Apple's signed apple_pay.cer back to Shopify
#
# For upload, also set certificate_id= (printed by create) and merchant_id= (the Apple
# merchant identifier, e.g. merchant.com.nwagtech.etch), and commit Apple's certificate to
# fulfilment/apple-pay/apple_pay.cer. That file is the *public* half — the private key never
# leaves Shopify — so it is safe in the repository.
#
# shop_domain and api_version default to the Etch store and 2026-07; override only if needed.

# First run with real credentials. status is a read: it authenticates with the client
# credentials grant and lists whatever certificates the store already has. If the token comes
# back, the app and secrets are wired correctly; if the certificates call is then rejected,
# that is the scope approval still pending, which is a different and expected failure.
action=status

certificate_id=
merchant_id=
